paragraphs: I've worked in Lamorinda real estate for a long time, and properties like 490 St. Marys Road don't come along very often. A gated lot of nearly an acre and a half, a creek running through it, no visible neighbors, and a home built by a contractor with enough pride in the work to choose every material himself  -  that's a genuinely rare combination for Lafayette. When I saw the listing come off the market without a sale after 31 days, I wanted to understand why, because the fundamentals here are real.

My honest read is that the listing strategy didn't do justice to what this property actually is. The description hints at something extraordinary  -  the custom finishes, the kitchen, the setting  -  but it never builds the picture that a buyer at this price point needs before they'll drive out for a showing. At $2,800,000, buyers are comparing carefully, and a listing that reads as a series of enthusiastic fragments doesn't give them the visual evidence or the narrative confidence to act. The home's story was there. It just wasn't told in a way that landed.

I've put together an analysis of the specific gaps I see and a blueprint for how a relaunch could be structured differently. It walks through the pricing position, the buyer profile most likely to move on a property like this, and the media strategy that would let the creek, the setting, and the craftsmanship do the actual selling.

If you're already working with an agent toward a new listing, please feel free to set this aside  -  no offense taken. But if you're still weighing your options, I'd welcome a short conversation. No pressure, no pitch  -  just a walk through what I've put together.

cover.tagline: The Blueprint for a Successful Sale

exec_summary.headline: A Custom-Built Creek Estate on 1.5 Acres  -  and a Listing That Never Showed It
exec_summary.p1: 490 St. Marys Road is, by almost any measure, exactly what the upper end of the Lafayette market is looking for. A gated, 65,340-square-foot lot with Las Trampas Creek running through it, no visible neighbors, a through-driveway, a three-car garage, and a home built by an owner-contractor who sourced premium materials and handled the craft personally. The kitchen alone was described as a showpiece. Each window frames the natural setting like a photograph. These are not manufactured selling points  -  they are genuine, defensible differentiators in a market where most homes at this price point sit on conventional lots with conventional views.
exec_summary.p2: And yet the listing came off the market in 31 days without a sale. The gap between the home's assets and that outcome points almost entirely to a strategy problem, not a property problem. The listing description read more like a contractor's walk-through notes than a narrative designed to move a buyer emotionally and financially. The visual media did not appear to capture the creek, the setting at dusk, the sense of privacy, or the craftsmanship detail that would have justified the price in a buyer's mind before they ever scheduled a showing. At $891 per square foot  -  the upper tier of the Lafayette premium range  -  buyers need more than enthusiasm. They need visual proof and a story that holds together.
exec_summary.p3: A relaunch of this property needs to accomplish one specific thing: give the right buyer  -  likely a professional couple or family relocating from San Francisco or the Oakland hills, drawn by privacy, land, and craftsmanship  -  enough visual and narrative evidence online to feel confident booking a showing. That is a solvable problem, and this home has all the raw material to solve it.

forensics.title: Friction #1: The Narrative Never Matched the Property
forensics.body: The listing description for 490 St. Marys Road gestures at something exceptional without ever delivering it. Phrases like 'looks like paradise' and 'saying WOW' are emotional reactions, not descriptions  -  they tell a buyer how they should feel rather than giving them the sensory detail that actually produces that feeling. At $2,800,000, buyers are reading listings with discipline and skepticism. A description that reads like enthusiastic fragments invites them to scroll past rather than book a showing. The creek, the privacy, the contractor-grade custom finishes, the kitchen  -  each of those deserved its own specific sentence, and none of them got one.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork listing remarks are written the way a great buyer's agent describes a home  -  specific, sensory, and structured to answer the questions a serious buyer is already asking. For a property like this, the description is the first showing.

forensics.title: Friction #2: A Premium Price Point With No Visual Proof
forensics.body: At $891 per square foot, this home sits at the upper end of Lafayette's premium tier. That number is defensible  -  the lot size, the creek, the custom construction, and the absence of visible neighbors are genuine premium inputs. But a defensible price is not a self-evident one. Buyers comparing this home against others in the $2.5M to $3M Lafayette range needed to see the creek from the deck, the light in the kitchen, the scale of the lot from above, and the sense of enclosure that makes the privacy real. Without that visual evidence, a buyer's instinct is to assume the price is optimistic rather than justified.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork's Sky Tour uses aerial video to show lot position, creek frontage, and natural setting in ways ground photography simply cannot replicate  -  giving buyers the spatial context that turns a price into a bargain rather than a question mark.

forensics.title: Friction #3: The Right Buyer Was Never Actively Reached
forensics.body: The buyer for a gated, creek-front, 1.5-acre estate in Lafayette with no HOA is a specific person  -  likely a professional or executive household, probably relocating from San Francisco or the Oakland hills, searching for land, privacy, and a home with genuine character. That buyer was not waiting on the open MLS for the right listing to appear. They were researching Lamorinda from their desk in the city, cross-referencing neighborhoods, and forming opinions before they ever contacted an agent. A standard MLS distribution strategy put this home in front of everyone equally, which in practice means it reached the right buyer only by chance. Thirty-one days passed without a sale, which strongly suggests that buyer was never found.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork runs geo-targeted digital campaigns that reach San Francisco and East Bay buyers who are actively researching Lamorinda before they've identified their target home  -  putting this property in front of the right household at the right moment in their search, not after they've already moved on.

positioning_table.verdict: At $891/sqft versus a benchmark range of $850-$920/sqft, this home sits in the middle of that range. At $891 per square foot, this home sits near the middle of Lafayette's premium tier, and the underlying assets  -  the lot size, the creek, the custom construction, the privacy  -  genuinely support that position. The issue was never the number. A relaunch needs to focus on building the visual and narrative case that makes $891 feel like the obvious price for what this property actually delivers, rather than a figure a buyer has to take on faith.

pillars.title: Pillar I  -  Tell the Story the Creek and the Land Deserve
pillars.body: 490 St. Marys Road has a setting that most Lafayette buyers have never encountered at this price point: a gated, creek-front, 1.5-acre lot with no visible neighbors and wildlife moving through it seasonally. That story requires more than a few enthusiastic phrases in the MLS remarks  -  it requires listing copy structured around specific sensory detail, written the way a buyer's agent would describe it to a client who trusts their judgment. The first conversation this home has with a potential buyer needs to make them feel what it's like to be there. BrightWork builds that narrative before anything goes live.

pillars.title: Pillar II  -  Show the Property From the Air and From Inside
pillars.body: The features that justify a premium on this home  -  the creek, the lot scale, the depth of the custom finishes  -  are invisible in standard MLS photography. A buyer looking at flat ground-level shots has no way to understand the spatial relationship between the home, the creek, and the surrounding landscape. BrightWork's 3D Matterport tour lets buyers walk the interior from anywhere, at any time, so the craftsmanship and the kitchen read as premium before a single showing is booked. The media package for a property like this needs to do the work of qualifying buyers before they arrive at the door.

pillars.title: Pillar III  -  Find the Buyer Who Is Already Looking for This
pillars.body: The household most likely to pay full value for 490 St. Marys Road is probably sitting in San Francisco or the Oakland hills right now, researching Lamorinda, and looking for exactly this combination: privacy, land, craftsmanship, and no HOA. That buyer responds to targeted exposure, not passive MLS presence.
